title: The Core of Data Quality & Governance

scenes.say: If your data can't be trusted, every downstream decision is at risk. So, what does it take to actually prove your data is reliable?

scenes.label: Quality
scenes.sub: Accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, validity
scenes.say: Data quality isn't just one thing. It's accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, and validity. Each one checks a different angle of trust.
You automate these checks with tools like dbt and Great Expectations. They run tests for duplicates, missing values, and broken links between tables.

scenes.title: Pipeline Metrics
scenes.say: Next, you monitor freshness and volume. If data's late or the row count suddenly drops, you catch it before users do.

scenes.label: Lineage
scenes.sub: Shows where data comes from and how it changes
scenes.say: Lineage tools map out how data moves and transforms. This makes it easy to trace issues back to the source.

scenes.question: Is masking PII enough for GDPR?
scenes.right: No—GDPR also requires consent, minimization, and user rights.
scenes.say: A common mistake: thinking masking is enough for privacy laws. But GDPR also needs consent, data minimization, and honoring user rights.
